# Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 + INT8 attention + INT4 MTP, FP8 PLE, **experts pruned 512 -> 384 (ARC-calibrated)**

This is the checkpoint `qwen38-flash-next-w4a16-mtp4-gdn8-qsa8` (see below for its quantization) with **25% of the routed
experts removed in every MoE layer** (512 -> 384, `num_experts = 384` in `config.json`). It was pruned for one use only:
the ARC-AGI agent workload (long reasoning + tool calls on grid puzzles). **Do not expect general-purpose quality.**
Please follow the base model's license.

## How the experts were chosen
- Routing was measured on 180 transcripts of the ARC agent running on the *unpruned* model (4.39M tokens, 2.82M of them
  generated by the model): the hardest 50% of 240 ARC train tasks (120 transcripts) + 60 of the 120 evaluation tasks
  (the other 60 evaluation tasks were held out and are NOT in the calibration data).
- Per layer the 384 experts with the highest score are kept, score = 0.5 * share of all tokens + 0.5 * share of the tokens
  the model generated. Kept experts are renumbered 0..383 in their original order and the router rows follow
  (`pruned_keep_ids.npy`, shape [48, 384], holds the original ids per layer).
- The MTP layer has its own router but no measured statistics; it reuses the keep-set of the last main layer (this can only
  change the draft acceptance rate, not the answers).
- Routing mass kept (share of top-10 selections that land on a kept expert, on the calibration data): mean 98.2% per layer,
  worst layer 94.9% (layer 0).

## What was measured (and what was not)
Held-out ARC evaluation transcripts (60 tasks, 174,591 scored tokens of the model's own last assistant turn), mean NLL:

| Model | NLL (nats/token) |
|---|---|
| Unpruned (512 experts) | 0.1826 |
| This checkpoint (384 experts) | 0.1875 (+2.7%) |
| (not uploaded) 320 experts | 0.2090 (+14.5%) |

- **The ARC agent solve rate of this checkpoint was NOT measured.** The unpruned model solved 52/86 test pairs (60.5%) on the same
  60 held-out tasks; no run of this checkpoint is available. NLL is only a proxy.
- Nothing was measured on general chat, code outside ARC, other languages or long documents. Expect degradation there.
- Loaded and served only on one NVIDIA B300 with vLLM 0.31.0 (Marlin WNA16 MoE); weights take 53.26 GiB on the GPU.
  Not run on 4x L4 / TP4 + expert parallel (384 / 4 = 96 experts per rank, divisible).

## Underlying quantization (unchanged by pruning)
All RTN (no calibration, no tuning), group size 128, symmetric, `auto_round:auto_gptq` packing.

| Part | Format |
|---|---|
| Routed experts (main layers + MTP head) | INT4 |
| GDN (`linear_attn`) `in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z`, `out_proj` | INT8 |
| QSA `self_attn` `q/k/v/o_proj` (12 layers + MTP layer) | INT8 |
| PLE n-gram table | FP8 E4M3 + one global BF16 scale |
| Shared experts, `lm_head`, `embed_tokens`, routers, hyper-connections, norms, indexer, `in_proj_a/b`, conv1d | 16-bit |

Size: ~100 GiB = ~47.7 GiB PLE table (pinned host RAM in vLLM) + ~52.5 GiB of weights on the GPU.

## Serving (vLLM 0.31.0)
```bash
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0
vllm serve <this repo> --served-model-name qwen38-flash-w4 --max-model-len 84000 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3
# 4x GPU: add --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel (plain TP splits the 640-wide experts to 160, not Marlin-friendly)
```
Do not pass `--moe-backend triton` (it also applies to the INT4 experts and Triton WNA16 rejects the router bias).
